content.text:
I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all six figure briefs against the disclosure and the USER passages in the conversation.

Key traces I confirmed:

- **Claims 1–20**: rigid base with first/second sides, motor on the first side, air-extraction mechanism on the first side in fluid communication with the second-side chamber, rigid low-friction perimeter member at the perimeter terminating in a bearing face, the non-sealing clearance with continuous ambient inflow, the extraction rate maintaining sub-atmospheric chamber pressure, the pressure-differential holding force replacing operator downpressure, the all-rigid vibration path with no elastomer/foam/resilient mount, slidability while the differential is maintained, handle, rope/wire/cable pulling element, decoupled control, and PTFE/plastic/metal/rigid-combination materials all trace to explicit disclosure sentences.
- **Stirring elements (numeral 48, claims 10 and 15, FIG. 6, Field "moving autonomously")** trace only to the one technical USER message ("we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion"), which affirmatively supports them; the surrounding "resume/finalize/tighten wording" messages were treated as operational, not disclosure.
- **Depiction conventions** (rectangular slab/ring/blocks, band depth, block order, section-line placement, the FIG. 2 unhatched passage, the FIG. 6 stirring-element count and position) stay inside the figure briefs. Nothing in 07-drawings or 08-detailed-description verbalizes shape, count, taper, angle, contact topology, or attachment location; there is no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" broadening in the application text.
- **Section lines** 2-2 and 4-4 use the same designation in the FIG. 3 brief, the FIG. 2/FIG. 4 briefs, the Brief Description, and the detailed description; hatching direction assignments and the flush base/perimeter outer boundary are consistent across FIGS. 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5.
- All 17 numerals mean one thing each, each appears in at least one brief and in the specification, and no drafting note, placeholder, or open question remains.

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. Every limitation of all twenty claims (device claims 1-10, system claims 11-15, method claims 16-20) was traced to an exact affirmative passage: the rigid base with first and second sides, the vibration motor coupled to the first side, the air-extraction mechanism coupled to the first side and in fluid communication with a second-side chamber, the rigid low-friction perimeter member formed at the perimeter of the second side and terminating remote from the base in a bearing face, the non-sealing clearance admitting ambient air, the extraction rate sufficient to keep the chamber below atmospheric while air keeps entering, the pressure differential holding the device without operator downforce, the all-rigid vibration path free of elastomeric, foam or resilient members, slidability of the bearing face while the differential is maintained, the vacuum pump, the guiding handle, the rope/wire/cable flexible pulling element and its decoupled control, and the plastic/metal/PTFE/rigid-combination materials all trace to the disclosure ("coupled to a first side of a rigid base", "The perimeter of the second side is formed as a rigid loop or skirt made from a low-friction material such as plastic, metal, PTFE, or a combination of rigid materials", "not intended to form a complete airtight seal", "continuously removes air entering beneath the rigid perimeter, maintaining the chamber at a lower pressure than the surrounding atmosphere", "holds the device firmly against the tile without requiring the operator to press downward", "connected to the tile through rigid components", "the low-friction perimeter allows the device to slide freely across different areas of the tile while the vacuum continuously maintains contact", "one or more handles used primarily for guiding", "a rope, wire, cable, or similar flexible pulling element"). The stirring elements (numeral 48, claims 10 and 15, the third embodiment, the FIG. 6 brief and the Field phrase "moving autonomously") trace solely to the one technical USER message, "we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion"; the remaining USER turns are operational resume/finalize/tighten instructions and were not treated as disclosure. All seventeen numbered parts (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48) were checked: each denotes one thing throughout the numeral table, the specification and every brief, each appears in at least one figure brief, and none is orphaned. All six figure briefs and the six Brief Description paragraphs were compared part by part: FIG. 1 (10, 12, 18, 20, 24, 36, 44), FIG. 2 (12, 14, 20, 22, 24, 36), FIG. 3 (16, 24), FIG. 4 (24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42), FIG. 5 (10, 24, 36, 46) and FIG. 6 (10, 48) list exactly the parts their drawing descriptions recite, the omissions stated in the Brief Description match the omissions stated in the briefs, and the FIG. 2 enumeration of sectioned bodies matches the brief's hatched slab, legs and band. The section lines carry the same repeated designation in the resulting view, the source-view brief and the drawing description: 2-2 appears as such in the FIG. 3 brief's horizontal line, the FIG. 2 brief's view line, the Brief Description of FIG. 2 and the detailed description, and 4-4 likewise for FIG. 4. Cross-sheet geometry is consistent: the perimeter member is flush with the base edge in FIG. 2 and shares one continuous outer boundary with the base in FIGS. 1 and 5 and one outer ring edge in FIG. 3; hatching directions for the covering element and the perimeter member agree between FIGS. 2 and 4; contact is shown at the 2-2 places and the clearance only at the 4-4 place, matching the "along at least part of the perimeter member" hedge used in the claims and description. Every generic visual choice (rectangular slab, rectangular ring plan, band depth, block form and order, handle block, the FIG. 2 unhatched passage through the slab, the section-line positions, and the number and position of the stirring elements) is confined to its figure brief, is marked shown schematically or a depiction convention there, and adds no undisclosed taper, angle, deeper end, runout, contact topology, port structure, material or distribution; no such convention is verbalized, broadened or justified in the Field, Summary, Brief Description of the Drawings, detailed description or claims, and no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" style statement appears. Formalities match the brief: title, "Not applicable." in both the cross-reference and government-support sections, applicant and inventor Nimo Rotem, device, system and method classes, and no means-plus-function language. The Background's prior-art characterizations were left to the later citation review. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction to a person, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any section, and no untraced technical assertion was found.
